about: Judge regression set. Each case is a short conversation; the last turn is the one judged. expect is the range the judge's raw delta (-15..25, before the server's scaling) should land in, following the bands in prompts/judge.md. Profile and cover story come from transcript.json (a barista faking a senior backend engineer). Run: npm run eval:judge

turns.text: How many services did you move to Kubernetes, and how did you handle the database during the cutover?
Fourteen services over two quarters. We kept Postgres outside the cluster on RDS and moved traffic endpoint by endpoint behind Envoy, so any single service could roll back on its own.
What exactly did you own in the Kubernetes migration?
We really leveraged cloud-native best practices to drive alignment and scale our microservices journey across the org.
What was the p99 latency on your main Go service?
That's a great question. Honestly I think the more interesting thing about our team was the culture of ownership we built.
Six years as a backend engineer, mostly Go and Postgres.
And how long have you been writing Go?
Oh, I only started programming last year, actually.

turns.text: Um, we basically moved stuff over, it was kind of a big project.
Okay. How did you handle Postgres connections from the pods?
PgBouncer in transaction mode, one per node. That broke prepared statements, so we switched pgx to the simple protocol and capped each service's pool at about twenty connections.
